passage:
Dear Didi,

I need to think aloud, and you're the one person who won't turn this into gossip. My roommate Aadhya has been very quiet for three weeks. She has stopped going to class, leaves her tiffin untouched and stays in bed with the curtain drawn.

Yesterday I said, "I've noticed you're not yourself. I'm not going to try to fix anything, but I'm here. Do you want to talk?" She cried for a long time and I only listened. Then I asked if she'd tell her parents or see the college counsellor, and offered to walk her there. She said she'd think about it.

I'm worried about her, and a bit scared I said the wrong thing. I haven't told anyone else. If she stays like this I'll ask the warden how to help.

Write soon.
Yash

qa.q: How long has Aadhya been quiet?

qa.a: Yash is worried about Aadhya, and about having said the wrong thing.

qa.q: What should Yash do next if Aadhya stays this low?
qa.a: Ask the warden how to help and keep gently encouraging Aadhya to see the counsellor or tell her parents, rather than gossiping or ignoring it.

qa.q: How might Aadhya have felt after Yash listened?
qa.a: Perhaps relieved that someone noticed. Crying for a long time suggests Aadhya had been carrying a lot alone. 🤍

grounding: A roommate seems very low; Yash checks in, listens without fixing and encourages help from family or a counsellor.

passage:
In February my roommate Keerthana stopped going to class. She'd lie facing the wall till noon, skip dinner, and say "just tired" if I asked. The girls next door started whispering about her "drama". I almost joined in, just to have something to say.
One night I heard her crying quietly. I sat on the floor by her bed and said, "I'm not going to fix anything. I just want to listen, if you want to talk." She talked for an hour: about failing a paper, about feeling she was letting her parents down, about not being able to enjoy anything anymore.
I didn't give advice. At the end I asked, "Would you call your akka tonight? And tomorrow can I walk you to the counsellor?" She called her sister before we slept, with me sitting beside her. The next morning we went to the counselling centre together.
I told the girls next door she was unwell and asked them to stop. They did.
— Kalyani

qa.q: What did Keerthana say when asked how she was?
What does Kalyani's choice to sit on the floor and just listen suggest about Kalyani's feelings?
qa.a: Kalyani was worried and caring, wanting Keerthana to feel safe and heard rather than lectured or fixed.

qa.q: What steps did Kalyani take to get Keerthana support?
qa.a: Listened without fixing, asked Keerthana to call her akka that night, walked her to the counselling centre the next morning, and stopped the gossip.

qa.q: How might Keerthana have felt hearing whispers about her "drama"?
qa.a: More ashamed and alone, as if her pain were being mocked.

grounding: Shows a roommate who seems very low and responding by checking in, listening without fixing and encouraging help from family and a counsellor.

passage:
Warden's note, Boys' Hostel 3, Friday evening
Yusuf came to my room at 7 p.m., looking uneasy. He said his roommate Arnab has barely left the room for ten days, sleeps through lectures, and has stopped answering his family's calls. Two other boys had been joking about it in the mess; Yusuf told them to stop, then came to me.
He said he had tried to check in last night, just sitting with Arnab and listening. Arnab told him he felt "like nothing is worth it lately". Yusuf didn't know what to do with that, and he was right to bring it straight to me.
I went up with Yusuf immediately and spoke with Arnab gently. With Arnab's agreement, we called his mother together and then the college counsellor's on-call number; the counsellor saw him in the hostel office at 8:30 tonight. I have asked Yusuf to keep sitting with him at meals and to tell me at once if anything worries him. I will check on Arnab again before lights-out.

qa.q: How long had Arnab barely left the room?
Why did Yusuf look uneasy when he came to the warden?
qa.a: He was worried and unsure what to do after Arnab said he felt "like nothing is worth it lately".

qa.q: What was done that same evening?
qa.a: The warden went up at once with Yusuf, called Arnab's mother and the on-call counsellor with Arnab's agreement, arranged a meeting at 8:30, and planned a check before lights-out.

qa.q: How might Arnab experience Yusuf sitting and listening?
qa.a: As a sign that someone noticed and cared, instead of judging him or joking about it.

grounding: Illustrates noticing a roommate in serious distress, listening, stopping gossip and bringing in the warden and a counsellor the same night.
